title: What the solver's log says about a hint

blocks.text: A planning service passes a solution hint on every solve and keeps each solve's log. Its dashboard should show, per solve, what the solver did with the hint. Write `hint_verdict(solver, log)`, where `solver` is `"HIGHS"`, `"GSCIP"` or `"CP_SAT"` and `log` is the list of log lines. It returns one of `"accepted"`, `"partial"`, `"repairing"`, `"rejected"` or `"unknown"`, from these lines (lesson 4.3.3 shows them all):

rows: `Attempting to find feasible solution by solving MIP for user-supplied values`
`feasible solution given by solution candidate storage`
`The solution hint is complete and is feasible`
`The solution hint is complete, but it is infeasible`

blocks.text: When a log has lines for more than one verdict, the first row of the table that matches wins: HiGHS logs a completed partial hint with both its "Attempting" line and a "MIP start solution is feasible" line, and that hint was partial. A log with none of its solver's lines is `"unknown"`: silence is not evidence either way. About twelve lines.

"""Run executes this file. Change the calls and see what prints. Submit grades."""
import logging

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")

from verdict import hint_verdict

print("HIGHS, start feasible:", hint_verdict("HIGHS", ["Presolving", "MIP start solution is feasible, objective value is 77"]))
print("HIGHS, start refused:", hint_verdict("HIGHS", ["User-supplied values of discrete variables cannot yield feasible solution"]))
print("CP_SAT, hint incomplete:", hint_verdict("CP_SAT", ["The solution hint is incomplete: 2 out of 9 non fixed variables hinted."]))
print("CP_SAT, hint infeasible:", hint_verdict("CP_SAT", ["The solution hint is complete, but it is infeasible! we will try to repair it."]))
print("GSCIP, storage line:", hint_verdict("GSCIP", ["2/2 feasible solution given by solution candidate storage, new primal bound 7.7e+01"]))
print("GSCIP, no hint lines:", hint_verdict("GSCIP", ["presolving:", "SCIP Status: problem is solved"]))

cases.says: a HiGHS log with an accepted MIP start reads as accepted, and one with the cannot-yield line reads as rejected
CP-SAT logs read as accepted, partial and repairing for a complete feasible, an incomplete and an infeasible hint
a HiGHS log that completes a partial hint into a feasible MIP start reads as partial
a SCIP log with no line about the hint reads as unknown, and one with the candidate line as accepted
